title: ERP workflow data — the state/transition document shape
description: The meta-schema every file under workflows/ validates against. A workflow here is data, not engine code: it declares the states a document family moves through and the named actions that move it, and the durable execution engine consumes it without owning it. This schema is a meta-schema rather than a document family — it declares no x-erp-document — so it has no lifecycle of its own. It deliberately does not pin the state NAMES: those belong to each document family, and pinning them here would make the meta-schema the place a doctype had to be edited. The structural invariants a schema cannot express (a unique initial state, no outgoing transition from a terminal state, reachability) are refused by names in integrations/erp/core/workflow.py.

schema.description: The workflow data dialect. Optional for a caller building the document in memory; every shipped file declares it.

workflow.description: The workflow's own identifier, unique across the model.

document.description: The document family this lifecycle belongs to. This is the join key: the asset gate requires a schema declaring x-erp-document equal to it, and a schema declaring x-erp-lifecycle requires a workflow declaring it.

version.description: The workflow data revision. Bumping it is how a lifecycle change is made visible rather than silent.

initial.description: The state a new document starts in. It must be declared in states and must carry docstatus 0 — the draft — which workflow.py enforces.

name.description: The state name. The lifecycle schema's state enum is the set of these, enforced as a parity invariant.

docstatus.description: The document status this state corresponds to, from the closed upstream vocabulary.

label.description: The display name a portal renders. Defaults to the state name.

terminal.description: Whether the state ends the lifecycle. A terminal state may have no outgoing transition — workflow.py refuses one.

action.description: The named action a caller invokes. At most one transition may leave a given state on a given action: two would make the next state undecidable, and workflow.py refuses that.

harvest: a document lifecycle expressed as states plus named transitions, rather than as engine code
each state carrying the docstatus it corresponds to
terminal states as a declared property rather than an absent transition
x-erp-provenance.note: The workflow definition shape, re-expressed as our own data dialect consumed by the durable execution engine. No upstream file was read into this repository; no upstream code, schema or text is copied or vendored.
